comparisons.peer_topic: Presentation of holding gains/losses in Level 3 rollforward
comparisons.peer_summary: Footnote (3) defines the amount of total period gains or losses included in earnings (and AOCI for certain securities) attributable to fair value changes for Level 3 assets and liabilities still held at the reporting date, specifically noting December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C define how net unrealized gains/losses are treated in the Level 3 rollforward for assets still held at period-end. GS states that 'Net unrealized gains/(losses) relates to investments that were still held at period-end' (gs_2024_8_P175_S003). Similarly, C defines this component as '(3)Represents the amount of total gains or losses for the period... attributable to the change in fair value relating to assets and liabilities classified as Level 3 that are still held at December 31, 2024' (c_2024_8_P810_S001). Both disclosures confirm that this specific metric captures only the gains/losses on positions remaining in Level 3 at the end of the period, excluding those sold or transferred out.

sentences.text: • Net unrealized gains/(losses) relates to investments that were still held at period-end.

(3)Represents the amount of total gains or losses for the period, included in earnings (and AOCI for changes in fair value of available-for-sale debt securities and DVA on fair value option liabilities), attributable to the change in fair value relating to assets and liabilities classified as Level 3 that are still held at December 31, 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment for Level 3 gains, losses, and securities valuation changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Net realized/unrealized gains and losses for Level 3 assets and liabilities are presented as increases or decreases to those positions. Changes in fair value of available-for-sale debt securities are recorded in AOCI (unless credit impairment), while sales gains/losses go to the Consolidated Statement of Income; unrealized gains/losses on MSRs are recorded in Other revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C describe the presentation of net realized and unrealized gains/losses within the Level 3 rollforward mechanics. While GS focuses on the reporting rule for transfers ('If an investment was transferred to level 3... its entire gain or loss... is classified in level 3' (gs_2024_8_P175_S004)), C explicitly details that 'Net realized/unrealized gains (losses) are presented as increase (decrease) to Level 3 assets, and as (increase) decrease to Level 3 liabilities' (c_2024_8_P808_S001). This highlights a shared methodology for incorporating performance gains/losses into the rollforward, with C providing the specific direction of the adjustment (increase/decrease) compared to GS's focus on transfer timing.

comparisons.peer_summary: Level 3 fair value investments increased to $4.0 billion in 2024, driven by $536 million in transfers in and $415 million in unrealized gains, partially offset by $123 million in settlements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose that transfers into Level 3 are a significant driver of changes in fair value, reported at the beginning of the period. GS states 'Transfers between levels... are reported at the beginning of the reporting period in which they occur' (gs_2024_8_P175_S004). JPM quantifies this by noting that Level 3 investments increased due to '$536 million of transfers in' (jpm_2024_8_P372_S001). Both disclosures align on the treatment of transfers as a primary input affecting the Level 3 balance, distinct from asset returns or settlements.

sentences.text: • Transfers between levels of the fair value hierarchy are reported at the beginning of the reporting period in which they occur. If an investment was transferred to level 3 during a reporting period, its entire gain or loss for the period is classified in level 3.

Investments classified in level 3 of the fair value hierarchy increased in 2024 to $4.0 billion, due to $536 million of transfers in and $415 million in unrealized gains, partially offset by $123 million in settlements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Level 3 hedge interaction and revenue inclusion
comparisons.peer_summary: Realized and unrealized gains/losses for Level 3 items do not reflect related gains/losses on hedging instruments in Level 1 or 2, and total gains/losses are primarily included in Trading revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS address the composition of gains/losses for Level 3 instruments, specifically regarding hedging. MS notes that 'The realized and unrealized gains or losses for assets and liabilities within the Level 3 category... do not reflect the related realized and unrealized gains or losses on hedging instruments' (ms_2024_8_P209_S002). While GS does not explicitly exclude hedging gains in the provided text, it defines the scope of its rollforward components strictly by holding status ('still held at period-end' gs_2024_8_P175_S003), implying a similar exclusion of offsetting hedges not classified in Level 3. Both disclosures focus on the standalone Level 3 performance metrics.

sentences.text: • Net unrealized gains/(losses) relates to investments that were still held at period-end.
